q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: SELECT f.bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS total_num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = f.bar GROUP BY f1.drinker ORDER BY COUNT(f1.times_a_week) DESC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM frequents AS f JOIN serves AS s ON f.bar = s.bar GROUP BY f.bar

explanation: Q1 and Q2 differ in how they determine the 'most_reg_drinker' for each bar. Q1 orders by 'times_a_week' in descending order and 'drinker' in ascending order, while Q2 orders by 'times_a_week' in descending order without specifying a secondary order for 'drinker'. This can lead to different results if there are multiple drinkers with the same 'times_a_week' value.
